watch.quality: Full-length scan. The metadata lists it as a silent film, also known as "Love and Sacrifice". It gives no score or restoration information.

editorial:
America is D. W. Griffith's 1924 Revolutionary War epic. United Artists released it on February 21, 1924, and Griffith's own company produced it. It is an adaptation of Robert W. Chambers' 1905 novel The Reckoning. The Internet Archive item, also titled "Love and Sacrifice", runs about 139 minutes. Wikipedia lists four credited cinematographers: George Bitzer, Marcel Le Picard, Hendrik Sartov and Harold S. Sintzenich. A creator can use the images freely. The print entered the US public domain by term on January 1, 2020, with the rest of 1924's works.

The trap is the music. The film is silent, so any soundtrack on a modern copy is a separate work. Wikipedia credits the original 1924 score to Joseph Carl Breil and Adolph Fink. A newer release may carry a different score, new intertitles or other added material, and those additions can be protected even though the 1924 images are not. Take the footage from a source whose score and titles you can clear, or add your own music. I found no restoration record, so I make no claim about one.
faq: Can I use footage from America (1924) in my own video?

Yes for the 1924 images. The print entered the US public domain by term on January 1, 2020. Check the copy you take it from for a modern score, new titles or other added material, because those can still be protected.
Does the source novel affect my rights?
No. The film adapts Robert W. Chambers' 1905 novel The Reckoning, which is an older work than the film. I did not find any claim on the novel that restricts reuse of the 1924 film.
